title: Fractions in Disguise: Percentages, Profit, Loss and Interest

standard_text: Percentages as fractions, percentage of a quantity, percentage increase and decrease, profit, loss and discount, simple and compound interest (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 8)
meta_desc: Class 8 Fractions in Disguise worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 1): percentages, percentage change, profit and loss, discount, simple and compound interest. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A percentage is a fraction out of 100
body_html:
How it works

A percentage is a fraction with denominator 100: 3/4 = 75/100 = 75%. To find p% of a quantity, multiply by p/100.

Percentage change = change ÷ original value × 100. A 20% increase multiplies by 1.2; a 20% decrease multiplies by 0.8.

Profit or loss % is on the cost price. Discount % is on the marked price. Simple interest = P × R × T ÷ 100; compound interest multiplies by (1 + R/100) every year.

Example

A phone bought for ₹8,000 is sold for ₹9,200. Find the profit %.

Profit = ₹1,200

1,200 ÷ 8,000 × 100

Answer: 15%

Example

₹10,000 at 10% compound interest for 2 years.

10,000 × 1.1 × 1.1

Answer: ₹12,100

Common mistakes

  • Working out percentage change on the new value instead of the original.
  • Taking profit % on the selling price.
  • Using simple interest when the interest is compounded.

faq.q: Why are percentages called fractions in disguise?
faq.a: Because p% means p/100, a fraction with denominator 100.

faq.q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
faq.a: Simple interest is on the original sum only; compound interest is also earned on the interest already added.

items.q: A school bag is marked ₹1,500. The shop gives a 10% discount. What is the selling price?
A shop buys a cricket bat for ₹400 and sells it for ₹520. How much profit does it make?
A shop buys a bike helmet for ₹200 and sells it for ₹220. What is the percentage profit?
items.e: Profit = ₹20. Percentage profit = profit ÷ cost price × 100 = 20 ÷ 200 × 100 = 10%.

items.q: A shop buys a backpack for ₹400 and sells it for ₹600. How much profit does it make?
A shop buys a pair of runners for ₹120 and sells it for ₹60. What is the percentage loss?
items.e: Loss = ₹60. Percentage loss = loss ÷ cost price × 100 = 60 ÷ 120 × 100 = 50%.
